{"sample_id": "blind-900a040a04b0476985d75941d050a573", "theorem": "Consider a prime $p$ of the form $4 t+3$. Show that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ iff $-a$ has order $(p-1) / 2$.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "number_theory", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "Let \(m=(p-1)/2=2t+1\), which is odd, and work in \((\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times\).

Suppose first that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\). Then \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=p-1=2m\). Since \(a^m\neq1\) but \((a^m)^2=1\), we have \(a^m\equiv-1\pmod p\). Hence
\[
(-a)^m=(-1)^m a^m\equiv(-1)(-1)\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)\mid m\). Conversely, if \((-a)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then
\[
a^{2n}=(-a)^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
Since \(a\) has order \(2m\), this implies \(2m\mid2n\), hence \(m\mid n\). Therefore \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m=(p-1)/2\).

Conversely, suppose \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m\). Put \(b=-a\), so \(a=-b\) and \(\operatorname{ord}_p(b)=m\). Certainly
\[
a^{2m}=(-b)^{2m}=b^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p,
\]
so \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)\mid2m\). If \(a^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then after squaring we get \(b^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Hence \(m\mid2n\), and because \(m\) is odd, \(m\mid n\). Write \(n=mq\). Since \(b^n\equiv1\),
\[
1\equiv a^n=(-1)^n b^n=(-1)^n,
\]
so \(n\) is even. As \(m\) is odd, \(q\) must be even; therefore \(2m\mid n\). It follows that \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m=p-1\), so \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\)."}
